gloss: to get along well; to be on good terms

definitions.gloss: to get along well; to be on good terms
definitions.explanation: to maintain a friendly and harmonious relationship with someone

definitions.gloss: to make friends; to become friendly
definitions.explanation: to establish a good relationship with someone, often used as an instruction or wish

examples.japanese: {兄弟|きょうだい}で{仲良|なかよ}くしなさい。
あの{二人|ふたり}はいつも{仲良|なかよ}くしている。
examples.english: Those two always get along well.

examples.japanese: {隣|となり}の{人|ひと}と{仲良|なかよ}くするのは{大切|たいせつ}なことだ。
examples.english: It's important to be on good terms with your neighbors.

examples.japanese: {転校生|てんこうせい}と{仲良|なかよ}くしてあげて。
examples.english: Please be nice to the transfer student.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めて{会|あ}ったのにすぐ{仲良|なかよ}くしてくれた。
examples.english: Even though we just met, they quickly became friendly with me.

notes:
A common expression frequently heard in everyday life, especially among parents and teachers speaking to children. The imperative {仲良|なかよ}くしなさい is one of the most typical things said to squabbling siblings.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {仲良|なかよ}くしなさい: get along (parental command)
- {仲良|なかよ}くしてね: let's be friends
- {仲良|なかよ}くしてあげて: be nice to (someone)
- {仲良|なかよ}くしている: to be on good terms

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {仲良|なかよ}し: close friend, being on good terms — a noun or na-adjective, often used by or about children
- うまくやる: to get along, to manage well — more casual and broader, not limited to relationships
- {付|つ}き{合|あ}う: to associate with — broader meaning including dating

WRITING:
Also written {仲良|なかよ}くする or {仲|なか}よくする. The kanji {仲良|なかよ}く is standard.
